REFERENCE BY THE CHAIR  
150th Anniversary of First War of India's Independence 
MR. CHAIRMAN: Hon. Members, we are commemorating the 150th anniversary of 
our First War of Independence. The year 1857 witnessed a great armed uprising against the 
British East India Company's rule in our country. 
Starting from Meerut, the revolt spread far and wide which inspired people to rise 
against the oppressive rule of the British. Enthused by their love for the country, thousands 
of freedom fighters laid down their lives for the cause of the motherland. We pay, today, our 
humble and respectful homage to all those martyrs. Their struggle and sacrifice gave 
inspiration to others which, finally, culminated in the Independence of the country, 
ninety years later. 
I request Members to rise in their places and observe silence as a mark of respect 
to the memory of martyrs of the First War of our Independence. 
(Hon. Members then stood in silence for one minute)

WRITTEN ANSWERS TO STARRED QUESTIONS 
NOC for allotment of lignite blocks 
*501.   SHRI HARISH RAWAT: 
SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) the reasons for which NOC is required from Neyveli Lignite Corporation for 
allotment of lignite block when Neyveli Lignite Cor poration is also a mining 
company and restricted to Tamil Nadu State only; 
(b) whether Government have any plan to withdraw this NOC system; if so, 
by when; 
(c) whether it is a fact that Government have allotted Raneri Lignite block 
of Bikaner district to Rajasthan State Mines and Minerals Ltd. and withdrawn 
the allotment on suggestions of NLC; 
(d) if so, the scheme of NLC to develop this block and by when; and 
(e) whether Government would allot this block again to Rajasthan State Mines 
and Minerals Ltd.; if so, by when? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COAL (DR. DASARI 
NARAYAN RAO): (a) The Neyveli Lignite Corporation ( NLC) is the major 
public sector producer of lignite and lignite based  power in the country. In 
addition to the existing mining and power generation activities in Tamil Nadu, 
the company is expanding its operations in Rajasthan. The company also has plans 
for development of blocks in open cast mining, underground coal gasification and 
coalbed methane in Rajasthan and Gujarat. 
NLC also takes up exploration activities in lignite  blocks in the country to 
augment lignite production. NLC is also designated as a data center for , lignite 
resource database. Therefore, keeping in view the f uture plans of NLC and to 
ensure that the resources are put to use in a plann ed and scientific manner, it has 
been provided that a State Government company or un dertaking shall obtain a 
certificate from NLC to the effect that they 
3 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2007] 
have no plan or willingness to undertake mining operation in the concerned lignite block. 
(b) The present arrangement is under review. 
(c) Yes, Sir. 
(d) NLC proposes to utilise the deposits from this block for an 
Underground Coal Gasification project, which was sa nctioned on 08.08.2005 
and it is expected to be completed within four year s from the date of 
sanction. 
(e) No, Sir, in view of the reply given to part 'd' above. 
Road network in NER 
*502.   MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR:       
SHRI B.J. PANDA: 
WW the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether it is proposed to allocate Rs. 50,000 crore to expand the road network 
in the NE Region; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) what is the action plan of Government to carry out similar activity to expand road 
network the most-backward tribal-dominated regions of Orissa to alleviate poverty of this 
region? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI T.R. 
BAALU): (a) and (b) An amount of Rs. 1142.8 crore has been allocated in the budget of 
this Ministry for 2007-08 for development of National Highways, State roads under the 
Central Road Fund scheme, strategic roads and roads  included under Special 
Accelerated Road Development Programme in North Eastern Region. In addition 
provision for the ongoing portion in Assam in the East-West corridor i.e. National 
Highways Development Project-Ill exists in the budget of National Highways Authority of 
India. 
(c) The Ministry is primarily responsible for development and maintenance of 
National Highways and selected State roads under the 
4 

[10 May , 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
Central Road Fund Scheme. Apart from the special programme like National Highways 
Development Project (which is taken up for the whole country) and Special Accelerated 
Road Development Programme for the North Eastern Region, the development of 
National Highways is generally undertaken through annual plans State-wise. No specific 
programme has been formulated for the development of backward region in the country. 
Development of State roads is the responsibility of concerned State Government. 
However, this Ministry gives Central assistance to develop State roads through 
Central Road Fund scheme. 
Autonomy to CBI 
†* 503. SHRI SHATRUGHAN SINHA: Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether Government intend to provide autonomy to the Central Bureau of 
Investigation in order to maintain its credibility; 
(b) if so, the action being taken in this regard; and 
(c) if not, the reasons therefor? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC 
GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS (SHRI SURESH PACHOURI): (a) to (c) The CBI has 
been accorded autonomy under the Delhi Special Police Establishment Act, 1946 as 
amended by the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003 for investigation of 
cases. 
Proposals for Four-laning of NHs in Rajasthan

Will the Minister of SHIPPING ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased 
to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that the State Government of Rajasthan have proposed four-
laning of NH-11 (Jaipur-Reengus-Sikar road section), NH-12 (Jaipur-Tonk-Kota-
Jhalawar road section) up to MP border, NH-14 (Beawar-Pali-Sirohi road section) 
and NH-8 (Beawar-Udaipur section);

(c) whether it is also a fact that the stretch between Chittorgarh to Neemuch of 
NH-79 qualifies for four-laning; and 
(d) if so, by when this stretch between Chittorgarh and Neemuch is likely to be 
four-laned? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI

(b) Four-laning of Jaipur-Reengus-Sikar section of NH-11, Jaipur-Tonk-

Development Project (NHDP) Phase-IIIA and four-lani ng of Beawar-Pali-

Report (DPR) of Jaipur-Reengus section and Jaipur-T onk-Deoli section of 
NH-12 is in progress. Bids for consultancy work for  feasibility study on 
Design, Build, Finance and Operate (DBFO) pattern o f Reengus-Sikar 
section of NH-11, Deoli-Kota-Jhalawar section of NH -12 and Beawar-Pali- 
Sirohisection of NH-14 are under evaluation. Four l aning of Beawar-Udaipur 
section of NH-8 is not included in any Phase of NHD P but it is proposed 
to carry out feasibility study on DBFO pattern for the same. It is premature 
to indicate target for four-laning of these stretch es since project reports 
are yet to be completed. 
Jhalawar-Madhya Pradesh Border section of NH-12, does not qualify for four-
laning. 
(c) and (d) Presently, there is no proposal for fou r-laning of stretch of 
NH-79 between Chittorgarh and Rajasthan/Madhya Prad esh border. The 
stretch from Rajasthan/Madhya Pradesh border to Nee much is not National 
Highway.

Statement 
A number of institutional arrangements have been made for ensuring proper planning 
and timely preparation for the Commonwealth Games, 2010. These include a Core 
Group of Minister (GoM) under the Co-Chairmanship of the Minister for Human 
Resource Development for coordinating the various works related to the conduct of the 
Games; an Apex Committee headed by Minister for Youth Affairs and Sports for 
overseeing and coordinating various matters related to CWG 2010; the Organizing 
Committee (OC) headed by the President, Indian Olympic Association for the conduct of 
the Games; and a Committee of Secretaries headed by Cabinet Secretary which is 
responsible for monitoring the implementation of the decisions of the GoM and taking 
decisions on other related matters. In addition to these arrangements, there is a sub-
committee under the Chief Minister of Delhi to take decisions in respect of all matters 
pertaining to infrastructure and other preparations for the games within the jurisdiction of the 
Government of NCT of Delhi. The Lt. Governor

security, law and orders and matters coming under DDA.

between all the stakeholders. All the stakeholders have indicated their specific time lines 
with reference to key milestones, viz., finalization of detailed design and 
estimates, commencement of tendering process, award of work, commencement of work, 
completion of work and handing over to OC. It is expected that work on all the major sports 
venue infrastructure projects will commence between June-August, 2007 and the venues will

concerned agencies/authorities to facilitate speedy clearances in respect of the games related

with clearances pertaining to Delhi Urban Arts Commission (DUAC). Keeping in view the 
need for developing adequate tourist accommodation in the context of the 
Commonwealth Games, an inter-ministerial Task Force has been set up under the Ministry of 
Tourism (MoT) for monitoring and coordinating further action in this regard by all the agencies 
concerned. A Committee for expediting the Central Government clearance in respect of 
Hotels coming in Uttar Pradesh has also been set up under Ministry of Youth Affairs and 
Sports. 
For preparation and to improve the performance of the Indian contingent for 
commonwealth Games, 2010, extensive discussion are being hold with all the

   *518.      SHRIMATI SUPRIYA SULE: 
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA BHARTIA: 
Will the Minister of URBAN DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Rs. 50,000 crore would be raised under the Jawaharlal Nehru 
National Urban Renewal Mission (JNNURM) to be spent over the next six years; 
(b) whether 12 projects have been cleared that are related to upgrading the water supply, 
drainage system and roads over-bridges of the respective cities; 
(c) whether about 63 cities, State capitals and 23 cities, which are famous for 
religious and major tourist spots have been taken up in the first phase; 
(d) what are the main proposals that are being considered; and 
(e) by what time they are likely to be implemented? 
THE MINISTER OF URBAN DEVELOPMENT (SHRI S. JAIPAL REDDY): 
(a) Yes, Sir. The Government of India has launched Jawaharlal Nehru National Urban 
Renewal Mission (JNNURM) on 3rd December, 2005 to provide reforms linked Central 
assistance for development of infrastructure in select 63 cities/Urban Agglomerations. The 
Government of India has committed Rupees 50,000 crore for JNNURM out of which an 
amount of Rupees 25,500 crore and Rupees 6400 crore have been allocated for submission 
Urban Infrastructure & Governance (UIG) and U1DSSMT  respectively for the 
mission period, i.e. 2005—2012. Matching amount of funds is to be contributed by the 
State Governments and Urban Local Bodies (ULBs)/Parastatals as per funding 
pattern envisaged in the guidelines. 
(b) No, Sir. So far, 210 projects have been approved for all admissible sectors under the 
sub-mission Urban Infrastructure and Governance (UIG) of JNNURM for a total approved 
value of Rs. 1773505.86 lakh. Out of these, 64 projects relating to Water Supply, 30 
projects in the drainage/ storm water drainage sector and 39 projects relating to 
roads/flyovers/ ROBs have been approved so far. Details of projects approved are placed at 
Statement I, II and III respectively. (See below).

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) Orders 
have been issued on 1.2.2007 for initial launch of the scheme for opening of 
franchise outlets in specified urban locations. The  scheme has already been 
launched in 88 identified urban locations throughout the country. 
(b) The scheme has been launched to provide better access to postal counter 
services in those areas where a post office cannot be opened as per the 
Department norms. Details of the scheme are given in the enclosed Statement (See

Statement  
     Details of Pilot Scheme for Opening of Franchised Outlets in Specified  
Urban Areas  
1. For providing increased access to postal counter services, Franchising Scheme 
was launched with effect from 1.2.2007 in 88 identi fied urban locations on 
pilot basis. 
2. Basic features of the urban franchise model 
2.1 Only counter services have been franchised, whi le delivery and 
transmission will be continued through the Departme nt. Linking 
arrangements for the franchised outlets will be pro vided by the 
franchisee. 
77 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2007] 
2.2 The franchisee will provide service across the counter for a 
minimum defined time schedule with flexibility to w ork round the 
clock. 
2.3 Products and services offered:  
(a) Sale of stamps and stationery. 
(b) Booking registered articles, speed post articles, money orders (on 
EDBO model), e-post, etc. (no bulk booking to be ta ken up in 
franchised outlets). 
(c) Functioning as an agent of PLI and provide related after sales service, 
including collection of premia (subject to fulfillment of criteria for 
PLI agents). 
(d) Marketing products for which the Department has a corporate agency 
or tie-up and provide related follow up services (subject, to agreement 
which the other organization involved). 
(e) Providing retail and bill/tax/fine collection/payment services of the 
Department (subject to agreement with the other org anizations 
involved). 
(f) Facilitating the provision of e-governance and citizen centric 
services (subject to agreement with the other organ izations 
involved). 
(g) Any other service introduced by the Department in future through its 
outlets which is considered amenable to the franchisee model (subject 
to agreement with the other organizations involved. 
The model has adequate flexibility built in to allow a range of services to be 
extended through the outlets according to the need/demand, and to increase the 
range when found necessary. Thus, the range of counter services that can be 
offered through different outlets can vary, keeping in view the location and its 
capacity to generate revenues. 
2.4 Implementation Strategy:  
In the initial phase and for the present, the urban  franchise model has been 
implemented only in fast developing areas of urban growth like metros and 
their satellite towns, as also such urban areas where there is a justification for 
post offices on the distance and population norms b ut there is difficulty in 
providing the same through redeployment. The 
78 

[10 May, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
further extension of the scheme can be taken up after the results available from 
experience of the initial phase say after six months of initial launch. 
2.5 Viability:—  
The viability of each franchise only requires to be assessed by the concerned field 
unit so as to ensure adequate returns to the franchisee. The expected minimum revenue 
would depend on the range of services, particular location, potential revenue, the 
investments that the franchisee is willing to make, the cost likely to be incurred by the 
Department in providing support facilities, etc. 
2.6 Criteria for Selection:— 
Applicants for franchises would need to submit an application in a prescribed 
proforma. The selected franchisee will sign a Memorandum of Agreement with the 
Department. Criteria for selection have been fixed considering the need to select persons 
with the capacity to manage and market a range of products, along with a sense of the 
community needs and public aspects of the job, and willingness to accept technological 
options. The criteria are as below: 
(i) Only individuals are eligible for appointment and not any organization 
which he/she may be serving/representing. 
(ii) Age: Above 18 years. No upper age limit. 
(iii) Educational qualification: 10+2 standard of 12th class pass of a recognized 
University or Board of School Education or Board of Secondary Education. 
(iv) Preference: 
(a) Postal pensioners 
(b) Those able to provide computer facilities 
(v) Premises: Proper appropriately located and accessible premises, properly 
maintained with suitable display of approved signages. 
(vi) Applicant should be willing to make the necessary investments for the 
conduct of the business and be able to provide a si mple business plan 
comprising details of how the premises will be . run, what the opening hours 
would be, investments proposed, market conditions, proposals for 
marketing products, awareness of customer base, role in local community, 
budget, 
79 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2007] 
finances, etc. Two references from respectable persons of the locality 
where the franchise is proposed to be located would  also be 
required to establish the character and antecedents of the applicant. 
(vii) A business plan would be prepared taking into  account the 
anticipated minimum level of business/revenue worke d out by the 
Devisional Head for the specific franchise. 
(viii) Security Deposit: The security deposit to be  provided by the 
franchisee would be based on the maximum possible l evel of 
financial transactions likely be undertaken by the franchisee in a day. 
The minimum security deposit would be Rs. 10,000 in the shape of a 
performance bank guarantee. 
(ix) Selection: Would be made by a committee comprising the Heads of the 
concerned Division and a neighbouring Division, based on a report 
from the Assistant Superintendent/Sub Divisional In spector 
(Posts).

Reduction in roaming charges 
3831. SHRI B.K. HARIPRASAD: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether a proposal from the Telecom Regulatory Authority of India is under 
consideration of Government with regard to reduction in roaming charges; 
(b) whether the Cellular Operators Association of India is resisting this move 
to reduce roaming tariffs; and 
(c) whether the COAI has contended that telecom tariffs  in India are 
among the lowest in the world and further attempts to regulate roaming tariff 
would force them to revise upward the regular tariff? 
81 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2007] 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS AND 
INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) to (c) The roaming 
charges levied by different operators have to be within the ceiling tariff prescribed by the 
Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI). TRAI, after due consultation process with 
all the stakeholders found justifiable grounds for a review of the tariff structure applicable 
for roaming services that had been fixed five years back. 
The Cellular Operators Association of India (COAI) had submitted that the customer 
tariffs are already lowest in the world and consistently coming down and thus, roaming tariffs 
should also be left to market forces. 
Based on in-depth analysis of various elements of cost, data on costs, views of 
stakeholders, the prevailing tariff for calls originated in home networks and other 
relevant factors, TRAI has prescribed a composite ceiling charges for regional/national 
roaming effective from 15th February, 2007. The Cellular Operators have already revised 
roaming tariff accordingly.

3852. SHRI SU. THIRUNAVUKKARASAR: Will the Minister  of

AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a)

up 48 centres across the country, the State wise ce ntre details are given in the

BPO course in Customer Support is of 160 hours duration having components 
of Computing Skills, English Language Skills, Soft Skills (imparted in 
English Language). The courses are being conducted in the North East, Jammu 
& Kashmir and also in DOEACC Centres at Kolkatta &Gorakhpur.

Research In Open Software 
3855. SHRI SITARAM YECHURY: Will the Minister of 
COMMUNICATIONS AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY be pleased to 
state: 
(a) whether Government are planning to fund the researc h in Open 
Software or Free Software; and 
(b) if so, the details thereof? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF COMMUNICATIONS 
AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) Yes, 
Sir. 
(b) The Government is promoting research in Free/Open Source Software area by 
supporting various institutions to foster research and development in this area. 
1. Under Indian Language Computing Initiative, National Roll Out project is 
being implemented by Centre for Development of Advanced Computing (CDAC). 
Under this project, the open source softwares such as Office suite, Browser, 
E-mail client have been localized for 10 Indian languages. The localization of 
these softwares for balance 12 Constitutionally rec ognized languages is 
underway. 
2. A National Resource Centre for Free/Open Source Sof tware 
(NRCFOSS) has been set up by CDAC with the objectiv e of development of 
F/OSS technology and solutions. The Centre has developed an Indian version of 
Linux desktop operating system (Bharat Operating Sy stem Solutions-BOSS) 
supporting Indian Language. 
3. National Informatics Centre (NIC) has initiated e-governance 
applications based on open source and open standard s like 
"Computerization of Police station", "Below Poverty  Line Database", 
"District Suite" etc. Also, specialized application  Collab CAD in the area 
of Computer Aided Design and Manufacture, based on Free/Open Source 
Solutions has been developed, which is being used b y major scientific 
organizations in the country. NIC has also started an Open Technology 
Centre.

(a) whether it is a fact that the mobile number portabi lity has been 
introduced in most of the developed and developing countries as one of the 
essential measures of enhancing the competition and  improving the quality of 
service; 
(b) whether any order has been passed by any of the jud icial/quasi judicial 
forums directing TRAI to introduce number portability in the country in respect of 
mobile services; and

implementation of mobile number portability in India?

AND INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY (DR. SHAKEEL AHMAD): (a) Mobile 
Number Portability has been implemented in some of the countries namely United 
States of America (USA), United Kingdom, France, Germany etc.

Redressal Commission, Delhi has directed the Telecom Regulatory Authority of 
India (TRAI) to "bring in 'NUMBER PORTABILITY RULE' as prevalent in the 
USA and other countries". TRAI has filed a petition before the Hon'ble Delhi High 
Court for setting aside and quashing the said order. 
(c) TRAI had submitted its recommendation on "Mobile Nu mber 
Portability" to the Government.

Statement-I 
Salient features of the guidelines for the districts component of the Backward 
Regions Grant Fund (BRGF)  
t The Backward Regions Grant Fund is designed to redr ess regional 
imbalances in development. The fund will provide fi nancial resources for 
supplementing and converging existing developmental inflows into identified 
districts, so as to (a) bridge critical gap in loca l infrastructure and other 
development requirements that are not being adequately met through existiang 
inflows, (b) strengthen Panchayat and Municipality level governance with more 
appropriate capacity building, to facilitate participatory planning, decision making, 
implementation and monitoring, to reflect local felt needs, (c) provide professional 
support to local bodies for planning, implementation and monitoring their plans, 
(d) improve the performance and delivery of critica l functions assigned to 
Panchayats, and counter possible efficiency and equ ity losses on account of 
inadequate local capacity. 
The implementing Ministry for the BRGF districts is the Ministry of Panchayati Raj. 
The Ministry has prepared and issued the guidelines for implementation of the BRGF 
recently. The guidelines have been placed on the we bsite of the Ministry of 
Panchayati Raj (http://www.panchayat.gov.in).  The salient features of the guidelines 
issued by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj are as follows: 
(i) The BRGF covers 250 districts including all the  147 districts 
covered by the Rashtriya Sam Vikas Yojana (RSVY). 
(ii) BRGF consists of two funding windows, namely, a Capacity Building Fund 
of Rs. 250crore per annum, and a substantially untied grant. 
(iii) The substantially untied grant will be distri buted among the 
districts as follows: 
143 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2007] 
(a) every district will receive a fixed minimum amount of Rs. 10 crore 
per annum, and (b) the balance allocation under the scheme will be made 
on the basis of the share of the population and area of the districts in the 
total population and area of all the backward districts. 
  (iv) All the 147 RSVY districts will be released funds till the plans 
approved under RSVY (plus the existing monitoring f ee) have 
 been completed to the extent approved. Non RSVY—BR GF 
districts will begin the process of District Plan p reparation in  
2006-07 in accordance with these guidelines. 
(v) Each Panchayat or Municipality within the backw ard district 
concerned will be the unit for planning under BRGF.  Plans 
prepared by each Panchayat or Municipality will be consolidated into 
the District Plan by the District Planning Committe e, constituted in 
accordance with the provisions of the Constitution. 
(vi) During the consolidation of the District Plan, particular care shall be 
taken to ensure that the District Plan addresses issues relating to SC/ST 
development. 
(vii) The State Government will designate a departm ent, preferably the 
Department of Panchayati Raj, as the nodal departme nt at the State 
level, responsible for the management, monitoring and evaluation of 
the programme. 
(viii) A High Powered Committee headed by the State Chief Secretary and 
consisting of members from various departments of State Government 
and the Central Ministries will consider and approv e the proposed 
District Plans to be taken up under the districts c omponent of the 
BRGF. 
(ix) All funds will be transferred to the consolida ted funds of the State 
Governments. Those funds that are to be transferred  to Panchayats 
and Municipalities by the State Governments will be  transferred to 
their bank accounts within 15 days of the release o f funds to the 
Consolidated Funds. 
(x) Audit, Inspection of works, preparation of booklet of verification of 
works and progress reports will be done as per the procedure 
prescribed. 
(xi) Separate guidelines have been provided in Chapter 5 for the States and 
districts not covered by Park IX and Part IXA of the Constitution.

3.3 Provision of Training: 
The objectives of the training component of Capabil ity building 
(Component 'd' in Table 1 above) are as follows: 
(a) Upgrading the knowledge and skills of all Panchayat s and 
Municipalities elected representatives to better pe rform their 
responsibilities. 
(b) Orient key officials associated with functions devo lved to Panchayats 
and who are working under or closely with them to e ffectively serve 
and facilitate the Panchayats in the performance of devolved functions. 
(c) Improve functioning of the Gram Sabha, particularly  through building 
the capability of pressure groups such as SHGs and CBOs to participate 
more meaningfully. 
Within the broad parameters of the National Capability Building Framework 
prepared by the Union Ministry of Panchayati Raj (A nnexe-3), State and 
District specific training strategies and plans sho uld be prepared by 
respective State Governments, which will be suitably supported by the

years, addressing the components described above may be prepared by each State. 
For this purpose, States may designate a nodal agen cy, such as the SIRD for 
preparation and management of the training plan. Technical assistance may be 
provided by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj for the preparation of State 
specific perspective plan document for training. 
The High-level monitoring and implementation committee at the State level 
may approve the plan before implementation. The costs can include both capital 
and revenue costs. 
Funds will be released annually by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj on the 
following conditions: 
(a) Receipt of the plan approved by the High level committee set up at the

(b) Indication of the funds proposed to be retained at the State level for

(c) An annual plan, drawn from the perspective plan, in dicating the

3899. SHRI RAVULA CHANDRA SEKAR REDDY: Will the PRI ME 
MINISTER be pleased to state:

168 

[10 May, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
(c) the steps to be taken by Government? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF PLANNING 
(SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN): (a) to (c) Yes, Sir. The Government 
recognises the importance of managing the population to achieve good growth 
rate by effectively utilizing available resources and improve the quality of lives 
of people. Stabilizing population is important for promoting sustaniable 
development with more equitable distribution. Howev er, managing and 
stabilization of population is a function of making child and reproductive health 
care accessible and affordable for all, increasing the provision and outreach of 
primary and secondary education and removing gender  bias, extending basic 
amenities including sanitation, safe drinking water  and housing, besides 
empowering women and enhancing their employment opportunities. 
The National Population Policy, 2000 (NPP 2000) pro vides a policy 
framework for advancing goals and prioritizing stra tegies to meet the 
reproductive and child health needs of the people, and to achieve net 
replacement levels (Total Fertility Rate, TFR) by 2 010. The immediate 
objective of NPP 2000 is to address the unmet needs  for contraception, health 
care infrastructure and health personnel, and to provide integrated service delivery 
for basic reproductive and child health care. The medium-term objective is to bring 
the TFR to replacement levels by 2610, through vigorous implementation of inter-
sectoral operational strategies The long* term obje ctive is to achieve a stable 
population by 2045, at a level consistent with the requirements of sustainable 
economic growth, social development, and environmental protection. 
Recognizing the importance of health for social and  economic 
development and for improving the quality of life, the Government of India 
launched the National Rural Health Missi6n (NRHM) i n 2005. Provision of 
accessible, affordable, accountable, effective and reliable primary health care 
facilities especially to the poor and vulnerable se ctions of the population, 
bridging the gap in rural health care services thro ugh creation of a cadre of 
Accredited Social Health Activists (ASHA), improved hospital care, decentralized 
planning, intersectoral convergence, maintaining gender balance and ensuring 
population stabilization constitute the basic features of the NRHM. The NRHM 
also includes the second phase of Reproductive and Child Health Programme, 
which intends to improve the performance of family welfare for reducing 
maternal and infant morbidity and mortality, 
169 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2007] 
and unwanted pregnancies. These initiatives are lik ely to provide the right 
impetus for improving the health & family welfare s ervices, and hasten 
process of population stabilization in the country. 
Sarva Shiksha Abhiyan (SSA), which is a national flagship programme of the 
Government of India, is the vehicle for operationalising the strategy for universal 
elementary education in the country. The programme seeks to open new schools 
in uncovered habitations, augment school infrastruc ture through provision of 
additional classrooms, toilets, drinking water, etc . The aim is to provide 
elementary education to all children in the 6-14 years age-group by 2010.

†3902. SHRI MANGANI LAL MANDAL: Will the PRIME MINISTER be

level for the year 2004-05 has been issued by the Planning Commission;

and Mixed Recall Period (MRP) method of Government are contradictory 
rather than uniformity; and

THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY Of" PLANNING 
(SHRI M.V. RAJASEKHARAN): (a) Yes, Sir. The Planning Commission has 
estimated the number and percentage of poor at national and state level for the year 
2004-05. These estimates were released on 21st March 2007. 
(b) and (c) The Planning Commission estimates the incidence of poverty at 
national and state level from the large sample survey data on household consumer 
expenditure conducted by the National Sample Survey  Organization (NSSO) 
at an interval of approximately five years following the methodology contained in 
the Report of the Expert Group on 'Estimation of Proportion and Number of Poor;' 
(Lakadwala Committee). 
On the basis of the latest large sample survey data  on household consumer 
expenditure (61st Round of NSS) covering the period July, 2004 to June, 2005 
[Report No.. 508 (61.1.0.1)], two different consump tion distributions for the 
year 2004-05 have been obtained. The first one from  the consumption data 
collected using 30-day recall period (also known as reference period) for all the 
items The other distribution is obtained from the c onsumer expenditure data 
collected using 365-day recall period for five infrequently purchased non-food 
items, namely, clothing, footwear, durable goods, e ducation and institutional 
medical expenses and 30-day recall period for the remaining items. These two 
consumption distributions have been termed as Unifo rm Recall Period (URP) 
consumption distribution and Mixed Recall Period (M RP) consumption 
distribution respectively. The Planning Commission,  using the Expert Group 
methodology has estimated poverty in 2004-05 using both the distributions.

associated technical aspects of procedures of measurement and data

3912.  DR. ABISHEK MANU SINGHVI: 
SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: 
Will the Minister of SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be 
pleased to state: 
182 

[10 May, 2007] RAJYA SABHA 
(a) whether the Merchant Shipping Act, 1958 enables Gov ernment to 
impound a ship registered in a foreign country, whe n there is a death due to 
negligence or murder of Indian sailors on such ships; 
(b) if so, the manner in which Government assures that our sailors get due 
justice whenever any serious physical injury or death comes to their notice suo 
moto or is specifically brought to their notice; and 
(c) whether the provisions of this Act of 1958 are adeq uate to protect 
interests of Indian sailors or whether any amendment is required? 
THE MINISTER OF SHIPPING, ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS 
(SHRI T.R. BAALU): (a) Any accident including the d eath or injury to any 
seafarer of any nationality on board a ship registe red in foreign country while 
the said vessel is on or near the coast of India ca n be invested by an officer 
appointed under section 359 of the Merchant Shippin g Act, 1958. During the 
course of investigation, the vessel or its crew can be detained for the purpose of 
conducting the investigation. However, if the death is due to any criminal act 
such as murder, the relevant provisions of the Indi an Panal Code/Criminal 
Penal code would apply and the Merchant Shipping Ac t, 1958 does not have 
any provisions to address such issues. 
(b) In cases where an Indian seafarer gets injured and dies on a foreign 
registered ship while the vessel is at high seas, i t is the jurisdiction of the 
respective flag administration to conduct investiga tion into the cause of such 
accident or criminal incident. The Government of In dia, being a substantially 
interested state, however, has now also started participating as observer in such 
investigation wherever possible. Further, whenever feasible, the Indian 
Embassy/High Commission officials are intimated to investigate the matter in 
the first port of call in the foreign countries. 
(c) The Indian Merchant Shipping Act address the subjec t of protecting 
interests of Indian sailors in various sections. However, to further strengthen the 
existing provisions following additional measures h ave been initiated by the 
Directorate General of Shipping. 
(i) Recruitment and Placement Rules, 2005 have been  notified to 
regulate various manning agents who employ Indian Seasfarers. This 
notification requires mandatory registration of such manning agents 
operating out of offices registered in India. This has ensured that 
manning agents, who employ Indian seasfarers on 
183 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2007] 
Indian as well as foreign registered vessels, are held accountable to the 
welfare of such Indian seafarers. 
(ii) A psychometric test has been introduced at the  entry level of 
officers in maritime training courses, which will help in determining 
his/her attitude and aptitude for the sea. It assis ts in taking 
corrective measures to mentally prepare for rigours of a life at sea. 
(iii) The Directorate General of Shipping has also made wide publicity in 
leading newspapers with regard to the recruitment t hrough the 
registered Recruitment and Placement Shipping Agent s for 
employment in marine sector. 
(iv) A new course module has been formulated to sen sitize the trainees 
with regard to rights of seafarers as laid down und er the Merchant 
Shipping (Recruitment and Placement) Rules, 2005 in  all Pre-sea 
Training Institutes. 
(v) The matter has also been taken up with the Inte rnational Maritime 
Organization (IMO) with regard to consolidating the  international 
conventions with regard to shipping casualty and ma king the law 
stringent to bring around the non-responsible flat state to carry out 
their responsibility. 
(vi) MS Notice No. 5-A has been issued by the D.G.S . This notice 
requires mandatory reporting and plan of action to deal with 
casualities involving Indian seafarers on foreign flat ships.

Development of NHs by Annuity and BOT method of funding 
3928. SHRI M.V. MYSURA REDDY: Will the Minister of SHIPPING, 
ROAD TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether it is a fact that Government had taken up t he development of 
National Highways by providing Government funds thr ough NHAI 
previously; 
(b) if so, whether there is any change in the policy of Government in taking 
up the Development of National Highways by Annuity and BOT method of 
funding; 
(c) if so, the difference between the mode of funding a mong these 
schemes (Government, Annuity and BOT); and 
(d) if so, in which scheme the cost of the project is less? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE MINISTRY OF SHIPPING, ROAD 
TRANSPORT AND HIGHWAYS (SHRI K.H. MUNIAPPA): (a) an d (b) 
Government has approved implementation of National Highways 
Development Project (NHDP) Phase III, V & VI under Public Private 
Partnership (PPP) on Build, Operate and Transfer (BOT) (Toll) mode. In case, 
the projects are not viable on BOT (Toll) mode under phase-Ill, then the projects 
would be taken up on BOT (Annuity) mode with the ap proval of the 
Government. If again, the projects are not viable on BOT (Annuity) mode, then 
the projects would be taken up on Engineer, Procure  and Construct (EPC) 
mode 
(c) Under Government funding, the cost of construction and maintenance thereof 
is borne by the Government and toll revenue (as per the per km toll rates fixed by 
the Government) on perpetuity is collected by the Government. 
Under BOT (Toll) mode, the Concessionaire is required to meet the upfront 
cost of the construction and the expenditure on ann ual maintenance for the 
concession period. Viability gap funding (VGF) limited to 40% is approved by 
the Government. The investment on project is recovered through 
209 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2007] 
toll revenue, as per the per km toll rates fixed by the Government, collected by the 
concessionaire and retained by them. 
Under BOT (Annuity) mode, the Concessionaire is required to meet the upfront 
cost of the construction and the expenditure on ann ual maintenance for the 
concession period. The cost of project is recovered  through Annuity payment 
(semi annually). However, the toll revenue is collected by the Government. 
(d) BOT (Toll) mode is advantageous to Government as the risk of traffic growth 
and recovery of revenue lies on the private entrepreneur who raises fund to build 
and operate the projects and therefore, lower Gover nment funding is required 
to implement it.

Next generation satellites for weather forecasts 
3938.    SHRI B.J. PANDA: 
MS. PRAMILA BOHIDAR: 
Will the PRIME MINISTER be pleased to state: 
(a) whether ISRO is planning next generation satellites  that are more 
effective in providing data required for making mor e accurate weather 
forecasts; 
(b) if so, the details thereof; and 
(c) to what extent this would "help provide reasonable prediction of 
monsoon and also help in disaster management system? 
THE MINISTER OF STATE IN THE PRIME MINISTER'S OFFIC E 
(SHRI PRITHVIRAJ CHAVAN): (a) and (b) Yes, Sir. ISR O is planning to 
launch an advanced dedicated meteorological satelli te INSAT-3D with 6 
channel high-resolution imager and 19 channel atmospheric sounder to provide 
temperature and humidity profiles, hitherto not available over our region for the 
meteorological community. Further, the launching of Indian Remote Sensing 
satellites, namely, Oceansat-2 with advanced Scatte rometer for ocean surface 
wind vectors measurements, and the Megha Tropiques with advanced 
payloads for providing information pertaining to water and energy cycies in the 
tropics should further augment the meteorological data services significantly in 
the next few years. It is expected that by around 2 009-2010, the full 
complement of Indian meteorological satellites will be in orbit and will be the 
state-of-the-art space systems. 
(c) With the advent of the full complement of meteo rological satellite 
systems, India will have a space-based synoptic obs erving capability for 
monitoring of weather related parameters such as cl oud structures, humidity, 
temperature and wind. While such advanced meteorolo gical satellites help to 
provide enhanced observational capability for improved meteorological services, 
an optimum combination of data from different sourc es including in-situ 
information is important to prescribe the atmospher ic state with accuracy, 
reliability, frequency and coverage. Towards this, efforts are also being made to 
augment the ground-based system such as LIDAR, Dopp ler Weather Radars, 
Automatic Weather Stations and Agro-meteorological 
217 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2007] 
towers. Assimilation of such vast amount of data into operational numerical weather 
prediction models is an important steps to improve the prediction of monsoons and 
aderse extreme weather events. Better understanding of the atmospheric processes 
will also help the disaster mitigation acivities fo r events such as cyclone, 
drought, and cloudbursts with timely early warning.

3962. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) the details of schemes implemented by Sports Authority of India (SAI) 
for spotting and nurturing of sports talent, promotion of sports in the country; 
(b) the quantum of funds incurred on sports promotion during the last three 
years, sports-wise/year-wise; and 
(c) the details of achievement made in international sp orts during the last 
three years? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI  
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) The details of schemes implemen ted by the Sports 
Authority of India (SAI) for spotting and nurturing  sports talent and the 
promotion of sports in the country are under:— 
NATIONAL SPORTS TALENT CONTEST (NSTC): The main objective of 
the scheme is to scout talent among school children  in the age of 8—14 years 
and nurture them by imparting scientific training i n SAI-adopted schools and 
'akharas' to achieve excellence at national and int ernational levels. SAI also 
provides coaches and special infrastructure facilit ies to these schools and 
akharas along with annual grant for purchase of sports equipments. 
237 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2007] 
ARMY BOYS SPORTS COMPANIES (ABSC): The objective of  the 
scheme is to scout talent in the age group of 8-14 years in collaboration with the 
Army and impart of them scientific training in thei r Centres to achieve 
excellence at national and international levels. Th e scheme, inter alia, also 
provides job opportunities in the Indian army. 
SPECIAL AREA GAMES (SAG): The objective of the sche me is to scout 
and nurture talent for modern competitive games and  sports from tribal, rural, 
coastal and hilly areas of the country and from regions such in sports talent, in 
terms of genetic and geographical characteristics/ advantages for excellence in 
particular sports disciplines. 
The main objective of the scheme is to train talented and meritorious sports 
persons in the age group of 14-21 years. Under the Scheme, the State 
Governments are required to provide land free of co st to SAI, while the 
development of the infrastructure is done by SAI. 
SAI TRAINING CENTRES(STC): Under this schemes, talented youth in the 
age group of 14-21 years are selected after assessment based on performance at 
national/state level competions and through a batte ry of tests. The selected 
trainees are given the option to join the scheme on residential or non-residential 
basis. The scheme is directly implemented by SAI. H owever, the state 
Government is required to provide the land and necessary sports infrastructure and 
other allied facilities like hostel building, etc. to the SAI. 
CENTRES OF EXCELLENCE (COX): The main objective of this scheme is to 
identify and train outstanding sports persons who a re medal hopes for the 
country in international competitions. The scheme o f Centre of Excellence 
envisages identification of talent in the country w ho has shown promising 
performance in the national competitions for furthe r training at the Regional 
Centres of SAI for nearly 200 days in a year. They are provided with state-of-art 
facilities, equipment and scientific backup alongwith specialized training. 
In all these schemes there is provision for payment  of stipend and 
medical/insurance expenses, kit and competition exposure. 
(b) Details of expenditure incurred on sports promotion under Plan during the last 
three years are as under:

Dismal scenerio of sports and games 
3963. SHRI MOTIUR RAHMAN: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS be pleased to state: 
(a) whether lack of sports culture in one of the major factors leading to 
dismal scenario in sports and games in the country; and 
(b) if so, measures taken to bring about change in the parental and societal 
attitude towards sports? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI  
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) With a view to rectifying the present state of affairs, the Ministry of 
Youth Affairs and Sports has been directed to prepare a "Comprehensive Sports 
Policy". This policy will address fundamental issue of making sports and games 
facilities available to the overwhelming majority o f youth, adolescents and 
children of our country who have hither to had no or little access to organized 
games and sports facilities at grass-root in villag e and urban India. The policy 
will also address the question of the integration of sports and physcial education 
with the formal education system. It is only through this broad-basing sports in 
the country, that it will be possible to promote excellence in sports in a scientific 
and well coordinated manner, 
239 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2007] 
spotting and nurturing talent from early childhood onwards. Besides, 
Government is proposing to introduce a nation-wide programme entitled, 
"Panchayat Yuva Krida aur Khel Abhiyan" aimed at pr oviding basic sports 
infrastructure, and popularizing sports and promoting sports competitions, at the 
grass-root level by synergizing the network of Panc hayats with a network of 
Youth Clubs and Sports Clubs, including those under  the management of the 
Nehru Yuva Kendra Sangathan.

3964. SHRI ABU ASIM AZMI: Will the Minister of YOUT H AFFAIRS

(a) whether it is a fact that there are no young players in the country for any 
game in the country; 
(b) if so, whether due to non-availability of young pla yers only old and 
outdated players are selected for international matches; 
(c) if so, the total number of cricket, hockey, footbal l, volleyball and

(d) the reasons for not selecting the young and new pla yers for better 
performance?

many national and international sports events. 
(b) Selections are the responsibility of National Sport s Federations, who

and fair manner with expert evaluations of the perf ormance of the shortlisted 
sportspersons. Many of those who are so selected are young sportspersons.

disciplines and particular events. These reasons cannot be generalized. 
(d) Does not arise as young players are, in fact, being selected on merit.

India's unsuccessful bid to host Asian Games 2014 
3965. SHRI T.T.V DHINAKARAN: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS 
AND SPORTS be pleased to State: 
(a) whether it is a fact that India unsuccessfully trie d to host Asian Games 
in New Delhi in 2014; and 
(b) if so, the reasons for failure? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI  
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) Yes, Sir. 
(b) It would appear from the outcome that the prese ntation made by the 
Republic of Korea carried more weight with the Electoral College than the Indian 
presentation partly because the RoK delegation said they would be showcasing all 
of Asia at Incheon, and not just RoK alone, and because they argued that such 
Games are awarded to cities not countries and Delhi had earlier been the venue 
of two Asian Games, in 1951 and 1982 respectively, whereas Incheon had not 
earlier hosted the Games. As the ballot was secret and no explanation of vote was 
required either before or after the vote, it is not possible to categorically state the 
reasons for which the vote was lost but it is to be  noted that the Chairman of 
the Olympic Council for Asia announced that the vote was decided by "a narrow 
margin".

3966. DR. K. MALAISAMY: Will the Minister of YOUTH AFFAIRS AND 
SPORTS be pleased to state:. 
(a) the causes for the utter poor performance of our Indian cricket team during 
the recent world cup series;

(c) the corrective measures taken in this regard; and 
(d) whether they would be effective and adequate? 
THE MINISTER OF YOUTH AFFAIRS AND SPORTS (SHRI MANI  
SHANKAR AIYAR): (a) and (b) The Board of Control fo r Cricket in India 
(BCCI), which is the recognized National Sports Fed eration for this sports 
discipline, has informed Government that it is of the view that the Indian 
241 

RAJYA SABHA [10 May, 2007] 
Team did not perform to its full potential and one bad game against Bangladesh was 
responsible for the early exit of Indian Team from the World Cup-2007. The BCCI holds 
the poor performance to be the collective responsibility of the whole team. 
(c) and (d) To ensure better performance of the Indian Cricket Team, the Board of Control 
for Cricket in India had organized a brainstorming session at which former cricket captains 
were invited and, in consequence, several measures have been taken which include intensive 
training inputs in different aspects of the game; norms in terms of minimum level of 
participation in domestic competitions; encouraging young potential players, etc.
